column2: Europa:Oh no…
Apino:Tzwii?
???:You're the last person I imagined I'd find in this place.
Europa:Draythus.
Draythus:I'm shocked you survived this whole time.
Draythus:You've grown.
Europa:You're exactly the same.
Europa:Same sword…
Draythus:…
Draythus:Tell me, Europa—how did you manage to befriend that unusual ghost?
Draythus:I've seen it before, but always at a distance…
Apino:Tzwii…
Draythus:How curious. Perhaps I should take a closer look.
Europa:Leave him be.
Draythus:I imagine he knows this place well.
Draythus:I have questions for you, little ghost.
Europa:I'm warning you, Draythus…
Europa:Whatever scheme you're up to isn't going to involve Apino.
Draythus:Rest easy. I will not harm him.
Europa:It's not the first time I've heard you make that promise.
Draythus:Oh, come now… I saved your life and my training surely saved it a dozen times again.
Draythus:You'd do well to be grateful for that.
Draythus:Besides, this is no scheme… This is far bigger than either of us.
Draythus:Soon the castle walls will no longer be able to contain the curse.
Draythus:The dark crystals will continue to spread, carrying the corruption and shadows with them.
Europa:How can you be so sure?
Draythus:Ha! Ask your friend.
Draythus:He seems to be keenly aware of the darkness.
Draythus:Isn't that right, little ghost?
Apino:…
Europa:That's enough Draythus.
Europa:We're done here. Don't come near us again.
Europa:Is that you, Draythus?
Draythus:The way is opening, Europa.
Europa:What happened to you?
Draythus:Do you know what this place was?
Europa:An orphanage.
Draythus:Most astute. It was a terrible place.
Draythus:I ran away as soon as the opportunity presented itself.
Draythus:But, in the short time I dwelt here, I discovered the truth. I learned what the sages of old foresaw.
Draythus:A curse, and the means to break it. Two halves of the same whole.
Draythus:For the longest time, I assumed that solving the mystery of the curse was my destiny.
Europa:…
Draythus:All the training I endured, everything I made of myself—it was all for this moment.
Draythus:And yet… something still eludes me… A final riddle I cannot figure out.
Europa:Maybe you're out of your depth.
Draythus:Haven't you been listening? There was a missing piece.
Draythus:And all this time, you've been keeping it so close.
Europa:This again?
Draythus:Don't you dare try to hide it, you little fiend.
Apino:Tzwii!
Europa:You've lost your mind, Draythus!
Europa:If you want Apino you'll have to go through me.
Draythus:It's finally crystal clear. I will be able to attain my glorious purpose. And you…
Draythus:You are in my way.
Europa:Even though there may be no going back for you, I'm not going to kill you, Draythus.
Europa:But I don't owe you anything anymore.
Europa:Let's go, Apino.
Draythus:Europa…
Europa:You are free from the corruption. Leave before it takes you again.
Draythus:To what end?
Draythus:It was not the darkness that consumed me, but my own ambition.
Europa:You're not the only person to lose their way because of the curse, Draythus.
Draythus:You assume I was ignorant.
Draythus:Yet I've known all along.
Draythus:All those years ago, at the orphanage. When I saw the vision of the sages it was you.
Draythus:You are the hero the sages foresaw. The final piece of the puzzle.
Europa:I am no hero.
Draythus:You will be.
Draythus:Europa, you must listen… consider this your final lesson from me…
Draythus:That little ghost you cherish so much…
Draythus:…and the foul demon who haunts this place…
Draythus:…they are the same being.
Draythus:They are the curse.
Europa:This must be Talos' Heart.
Europa:It's in terrible shape—the shadows have nearly consumed it.
Apino:Tzwiiii!
Europa:I know it's dangerous, but if we do nothing the castle will collapse.
Europa:Come on, Apino. Please… trust me.
Apino:Tzwiii!
Europa:I… I think we just saved Talos.
Apino:Tzwii.
Europa:Yes. Thank you for trusting me.
Europa:Having you around isn't so bad, you know?
Europa:I haven't been very grateful to you.
Europa:I just… have a hard time opening up to others.
Europa:I don't know, it's just… seems like every time I trust someone I end up hurt by them.
Europa:I'm… tired from it.
Europa:But thank you for sticking with me.
Europa:You are quite a brave little bear, I must say.
Apino:Tzwiwiwiwiwi!
Europa:I like you too, Apino.
Apino:Tzwii! Tzwii!
Europa:Come on, let's go.
Europa:That hammer is definitely not a good sign, Apino.
Europa:So let's just get this over with.
Europa:That hammer is definitely not a good sign.
Europa:So let's get this over with.
Europa:I wonder how long he was trapped in here before the curse claimed his mind…
Frinise:My, my! Look at you! What is your name, darling?
Europa:…I'm Europa.
Frinise:And aren't you beautiful, Europa!
Europa:…Thank you?
Frinise:You're surely used to hearing such things, though.
Europa:I don't—
Frinise:Everyone is kind to beautiful people like you.
Frinise:Kind and generous.
Frinise:People were never generous with me. I had no money, so they threw me out.
Frinise:But I was able to make a bargain to save myself…
Frinise:And all it cost was my soul.
Europa:You traded one debt for another.
Frinise:Don't be so silly. Before, I was nobody. Now look at me! I can take anything I want.
Frinise:Is there anything valuable you would like to be generous with, Europa?
Frinise:How sad. Beautiful people never share their beautiful things!
Europa:I wonder what will happen to her. She traded away her soul…
Europa:She was so full of hatred. Maybe she'll find peace now that she's free of that body.
Europa:I wonder what will happen to her now.
Europa:I hope her soul can find peace. Wherever it is.
Europa:The crystal in that machine looks like the geodes we've seen around Talos. It looks corrupted, though.
Europa:The curse has twisted it into a deadly abomination.
Europa:No… we can't run. We must destroy it.
Europa:The crystal in that machine looks like the geodes I've seen around Talos. It looks corrupted, though.
Europa:The curse has twisted it into a deadly abomination…
Europa:It's too dangerous to leave intact.
Europa:The world is a better place without that awful machine.
Horned God:Ahh, it has been many moons since I crossed paths with such a young soul.
Horned God:How is it that I have not met you until now, child?
Europa:I only recently came here.
Horned God:And you've brought another soul with you! One with purity beyond compare.
Horned God:I must have it.
Apino:Tz-wii…
Europa:Don't you dare touch him.
Horned God:Such purity before me. Worry not, for I will set you free. You will know peace.
Europa:Apino, we're leaving!
Horned God:Foolish child!
Europa:We don't need you to set us free!
Horned God:It is my duty to protect your souls, and I will fulfill it!
Europa:I only recently came here. But who are you?
Horned God:A protector of delicate little souls. Unique souls, such as your own.
Europa:I'm no different from anyone else.
Horned God:No, I can see it clearly. Your soul carries the weight of suffering—yet it also reminds me of the children who once lived here.
Europa:There were children here? What happened to them?
Horned God:I was able to save some of them, but most… went away… when the dark magic claimed the castle.
Europa:How did you save them? Where—
Horned God:Pain weighs on your soul. Worry not. You will know peace once more.
Horned God:I will give your soul rest from the weariness that crushes it.
Europa:I'm not offering you my soul.
Horned God:I will not allow you to reject my wisdom. Let me end your suffering, child!
Europa:He didn't protect souls, he held them captive.
Europa:It's alright; he won't do it again. We made sure of that.
Europa:Now they are finally free.
Issa:Howdy, ma'am.
Issa:You wouldn't mind lending me a hand, would you?
Europa:…That depends.
Issa:Don't worry, I won't be needing much of your time.
Issa:The thing is… I've been on the road a long time. I heard stories about this place along the way.
Issa:None that I believed, mind you, but I still thought I should take a peek around here.
Europa:What did you find out?
Issa:Well, the story about the mechanical giant turned out to be true.
Issa:And seeing all that fine metalwork got me thinking about another story I heard…
Issa:A story about armor forged by the first craftsmen with power beyond compare.
Issa:You see, I have something of an interest in ancient artifacts. I reckon I'd know one if I saw it in person.
Issa:Why don't you tell me exactly where you found that armor? I have a client who would pay good money for it.
Europa:That's none of your business.
Issa:There's no need to make things difficult, sweetheart. You don't want to do that.
Europa:You know what? I think I might.
Issa:Listen, girl, I didn't come all this way just to leave empty-handed!
Europa:I wish I could help you, but I don't know anything about artifacts.
Issa:Looks to me like you're wearing one right now.
Issa:Just hand over that armor and we'll call it even. No need for any trouble.
Europa:I disagree.
Issa:I guess we're doing this the hard way then.
Europa:What annoys me most…
Europa:…is that he said he wouldn't waste my time.
Europa:Apino, you've heard the legend of Leno, haven't you?
Europa:This beast looks just like him.
Europa:I never believed the stories, yet here he is.
Europa:A beast that lives in a pit of garbage and hurls tomatoes…
Europa:It's fine. The stories surely exaggerated his strength.
Europa:When I was a child, I was told stories about a creature named Leno.
Europa:I never believed they were true, yet here you are.
Europa:How dangerous could you possibly be?
Europa:Only one way to find out…
Europa:I can't believe it. It was all true.
Europa:Well, now that he's been dealt with, I certainly won't miss the smell.
Nissi:No, no, Limo! Listen! Nissi already explain! Limo no have feet, so no shoes for Limo.
Limo:Limo want shoes. Limo put on hands.
Nissi:Shoes no work on hands.
Limo:Okay…
Limo:Limo put socks on hands?
Apino:Tz-tzwii?
Europa:I don't know what to think either.
Limo:Oh no! Whooooop whooooop! Danger! Danger!
Nissi:An attack! A trick! A trap!
Limo:Lady eat us!
Europa:Hey, calm down! This isn't a trap.
Europa:What kind of creature are you? You look…
Europa:Yeah, gooey.
Nissi:RUDE. Nissi fight!
Nissi:Defeat lady with scary weapon and her pet ghost!
Europa:Don't take it personally, Apino, they're just scared.
Limo:Limo will help Nissi fight! Make rude lady and ghost go away!
Nissi:Nissi take front! Armor stop scary weapon!
Europa:Wait, are we seriously fighting?
Nissi:We no taste gooooooood!
Europa:That was… different. I feel bad leaving them like that. They were kind of cute.
Europa:We should get out of here before they, um… slime themselves back together again.
Link:Look, we found another one.
Link:I doubt it. Huntresses never wear armor.
Europa:Who are you talking to?
Link:You dare to question us? You are the one who will give answers.
Link:Where is the rest of your clan?
Europa:I don't belong to any clan, and I don't know which huntresses you mean!
Link:Curious.
Link:A huntress would never deny her clan. Maybe she's telling us the truth?
Europa:Who are… all of you?
Link:We are many.
Link:Linked together by one purpose: to destroy the huntress clan.
Link:By our master's command, the huntresses will never obtain the power they seek!
Europa:How many of you are there?
Link:We are seven. One for each huntress.
Link:Enough of her questions!
Link:She could take this information back to her clan.
Link:We can't risk letting her escape! One life is a small price to pay if we are wrong.
Europa:Those huntresses owe me one.
Europa:Is this a man or a machine?
Europa:The last time I saw this game, I was a little girl. My father would play chess with me.
Europa:The rules seem different this time…
Europa:I could never beat my father whenever we played.
Europa:But he did give me practice against a more skilled opponent.
Europa:Still… maybe this version is a better fit for my talents.
???:Stop right there!
???:Who are you?
Europa:And I'm Europa.
???:You would do well to leave, Europa. The curse runs thick here.
Europa:Who are you?
Miria:The last guardian of this castle. Call me Miria.
Europa:If the curse runs thick you shouldn't be lingering here, Miria.
Miria:My duties require that I stay. With my sister fallen, the burden is mine alone.
Europa:What happened?
Miria:One of the other guardians violated their oath and betrayed us.
Miria:Apparently one of the magical artifacts here was worth more than their honor. Or Dina's life.
Miria:I see you've collected several for yourself as well.
Miria:You have looted my home, Europa.
Europa:I-
Miria:My lack of vigilance cost me my sister. You're a fool if you think I haven't learned from that mistake.
Europa:I'm just here to help!
Europa:Yes, you're right, Apino!
Europa:Miria, the curse is affecting you.
Miria:Lies from the mouth of a thief!
Miria:Wait!
Miria:I yield, just… please… don't kill me! Talos is overrun with monsters and villains and the curse continues to spread!
Miria:If I am dead then monsters will storm the theater just like they did the orphanage!
Miria:Europa, there is no one else left protecting this place or the innocent people still alive!
Europa:I don't want to kill you, Miria.
Europa:I am not your enemy. We want the same thing.
Miria:I…
Miria:I believe you… It's just…
Miria:I don't know what's been happening to me. I feel like I'm going mad. I can't think clearly.
Europa:It's time to forgive yourself for your failures.
Europa:You have honored your sister and your heritage as a guardian. They would be proud of you.
Miria:…I hope so.
Europa:What kind of creature is this?
Europa:I feel cold…
Europa:Stay away from us!
Europa:Who are you, monster?
Europa:That thing won't be taking any more lives.
Europa:Yeah, I feel warmer too.
Europa:…and I'm beginning to feel warm again.
???:Finally, a proper meal!
Apino:TZWII!
???:One strike from my axe should be enough for a tiny thing like you.
Europa:Try it.
???:Hahaha! Tiny words from the tiny creature!
???:You dare to challenge me?
Europa:Who said it would be a challenge?
Ulf:You poor, tiny fool! I am the great Ulf!
Ulf:Descendant of the ancient Tribe of the White Lands, and heir to their legacy!
Ulf:Through my glory I honor their memory and it lives eternal!
Europa:And you do this by eating people.
Ulf:Again, you mock me!
Ulf:None in this kingdom have withstood the might of the great Ulf!
Ulf:The goddess Hel herself has given me the power to win every battle!
Europa:Never heard of her. Or you.
Ulf:Then you will bear witness to her power!
Ulf:Your blasphemous bones will make a fine offering!
Ulf:I am the great Ulf!
Ulf:I will bring glory and honor to their memory!
Europa:And you plan to do this by eating people.
Ulf:Again, you mock me, but none in this kingdom have withstood the might of the great Ulf!
Ulf:Then you will bear witness to her power.
Europa:I guess the goddess Hel was fed up with him.
???:Hey! We haven't seen each other for a long time.
???:You brought company.
Europa:Do you know each other?
Apino:Tzwii-wiii…
Bebel:My name is Bebel. You're new here, right? I haven't seen your pretty face before.
Europa:Yes, I just got here.
Bebel:Oh sweetie… bad idea. This place is awful.
Bebel:It was even worse before the color came back.
Europa:What are you doing here?
Bebel:I was washing my crystals near the waterfalls when I heard a horrible growl.
Bebel:I don't dare return. I have no desire to find out what was making that noise, thank you very much.
Bebel:Do you think… maybe you could help me get rid of whatever monster is lurking back there?
Europa:Sure, I'll be on the lookout.
Bebel:Thank you! And you, little one, would you like to go to the theater with me?
Europa:Apino and I have things to do, but we'll let you know when we've dealt with the monster.
Bebel:Alright then. I’ll be waiting to hear from you.
Europa:I might have done that already.
Europa:It was tall, menacing, and had a skull over its head.
Bebel:Well, that must have been it! It sounds like the right amount of dreadful.
Bebel:Please have this, as thanks. I can't wait to go back to the waterfall!
Apino:Tzwii!!
Europa:Uh, hello. Who are you?
Bebel:My name is Bebel. You're new here, right? I'm sure I haven't seen your pretty face before.
Bebel:Thank you! And be sure to come see me at the theater.
Bebel:Don't forget about me, alright?
Europa:I'll let you know when I've dealt with the monster.
Bebel:I see you’re still here. I hope you're being careful.
Europa:As careful as I can be in a place full of monsters.
Bebel:Ugh, please. Don’t remind me…
Bebel:So, you've been looking for the rest of the orchestra, right?
Europa:More like bumping into them.
Bebel:Oh well…
Bebel:Still, thank you for helping us.
Europa:It is done. The growling creature will trouble you no more.
Bebel:My hero! Thank you so much.
Bebel:I can't imagine how hard it was to get rid of him. This is for you.
Europa:It's beautiful, thank you.
Europa:It is done. The creature will trouble you no more.
Bebel:I can't imagine how hard it was to get rid of that monster. This is for you.
Bebel:I was beginning to believe you wouldn’t come.
Bebel:Did you find the growling creature?
Bebel:This theater is beautiful. I love being here!
Bebel:No one interrupts me here with silly growls.
Bebel:You should get some rest! You look exhausted, sweetie.
Bebel:You can stay here with me.
Michiru:Safe travels, Europa.
Michiru:We will be here if you need us.
Michiru:Young warrior, we've done everything in our power to help you.
Michiru:You must continue on your own now.
Europa:I will, thank you.
Michiru:How are you feeling, young warrior? Let us see what you have found.
Michiru:Well done. Now we shall guide you.
Michiru:It seems you do not have enough notes at the moment. Keep looking, young warrior.
Michiru:We trust that you will be able to find the magic we need.
Michiru:Remember to look for the music notes! You never know where they might be.
???:Welcome, young warrior. We are glad you are finally here.
Europa:You knew I was coming?
???:Indeed, long have we waited for you.
???:With your arrival comes the time to witness all that was foreseen by the ancient builders of this castle.
Europa:I don't understand. Who are you?
Michiru:My name is Michiru, and this is my sister Kahori.
Michiru:Forgive her for her silence, for she is not a talkative being—she keeps her voice for her songs.
Michiru:You can find Master Hibino at the end of the hall as well.
Michiru:We will help you heal. Not only physical wounds, but also those of your heart and mind.
Europa:What do you mean?
Michiru:We are composers from the Dorian era, sent by the gods to heal the world with our music.
Europa:Now would be a good time to start. The world is a mess and it has been for years.
Michiru:That duty falls to another. We have a different role to play.
Michiru:Furthermore, we have been lacking our source of divine magic.
Michiru:There are music notes scattered around the castle. We need them to carry out our duty.
Michiru:Have you found any notes during your travels so far?
Europa:I have.
Michiru:Keep looking, young warrior.
Kondor:Hi! We've been worried about you.
Europa:I'm fine. I found the source of your nightmares.
Europa:You were right—it was a creature that fed on people's fears.
Kondor:Oh gods, how awful! Is it still lurking around the castle?
Europa:No, I took care of it. It won't disturb anyone again.
Kondor:I expect you've been through a lot, and yet you were brave for our sakes. We want to thank you.
Europa:Really, you don't have to–
Kondor:I insist! We have been rehearsing, and we are ready to present our concert! And you…
Kondor:…you are the guest of honor.
???:Are you… real?
Europa:Yes, I am. Are you alright?
???:This place has been playing tricks on me. I feel like I'm losing my mind.
Kondor:…Kondor.
Kondor:How strange… I can barely remember my own name right now.
Kondor:I went looking for my musicians and I got lost. The rest of the memory is just a blur. I wonder how long it's been.
Kondor:The truth is, I'm the one to blame if anything happens to them. It was my idea to come here in the first place.
Kondor:I wanted us to play in the famous Theater of Talos, the greatest of honors. I never thought we would be trapped here like this…
Kondor:I should never have let the musicians wander around the castle alone.
Europa:Don't blame yourself for their choice to wander off.
Europa:You can still fulfill your dream to play music in this castle, but not if you give up and die here.
Kondor:I would like that very much. I… should go then, I suppose. Thank you so much for your help.
Kondor:Oh, and one more piece of advice. Please, do not stay in this place too long.
Kondor:I woke myself out of a nightmare last night, and it all seemed so real. I'm not sure we're alone here.
Europa:Head to the theater. Maybe you can get some rest there.
Kondor:Yes… good idea… I'll try to get some sleep in the theater.
Kondor:I may need your help with another matter later. Please visit me in the theater if you have the time.
Kondor:Thank you for your help, Europa.
Kondor:You were right. Despite everything, my dream was fulfilled.
Kondor:We all hope that you enjoyed our concert.
Kondor:I feel much better now that I finally got some rest.
Kondor:There was something—or someone—that kept me from sleeping. I wonder what it was.
Kondor:I wanted to thank you for the help; some of my musicians came back. I'm so relieved!
Kondor:Please, if you find anyone else lost out there, help them get back to the theater.
Kondor:Almost everyone has made it back here! I hope the rest are alright… It's very easy to get lost in this place.
Kondor:This is the most talented orchestra I've ever conducted. I hope you can bring back the rest of them!
Kondor:You have been very kind to us, Europa. Let me express our gratitude, on behalf of everyone here.
Kondor:We should not have wandered about the castle without thinking things through first.
Europa:What matters most is that everyone is safe. I'm glad I could help.
Kondor:Still, this curse seems far from over, even though Talos is stronger than ever.
Kondor:Do you remember the nightmares I told you about? Several of my musicians started experiencing them too.
Kondor:They felt like they were being watched, and their dreams were full of disturbing thoughts.
Kondor:I wonder if this is all related to the noises we've been hearing up in the towers. It can't be anything good.
Europa:I'll take a look and see what I can find. Don't leave the theater, alright?
Kondor:Of course. Thank you, Europa.
Kondor:You found all the musicians! They're finally safe, and my orchestra is complete! I am truly grateful, Europa.
Kondor:They've been sharing what they've gone through, it's a shame they've all lost such important belongings.
Kondor:Please let us know when you clear the way so that they can go retrieve their things.
Kondor:The musicians are restless. They want the castle to be safe again.
Kondor:I just can't seem to get my musicians to start rehearsing.
Kondor:They all seem so distracted…
Kondor:If they could safely retrieve their missing keepsakes I think it would help them find some peace of mind.
Hibino:I've done everything I can to help you.
Hibino:The rest is up to you.
Hibino: Good luck, young warrior.
Europa:Thank you, Hibino.
???:Welcome to my workshop.
Europa:A workshop next to a music theater?
???:For my art there is no better place.
Hibino:I'm Hibino.
Hibino:I suppose you met Michiru and Kahori on the way here. We are on a special mission.
Hibino:In fact, we've been awaiting your arrival. We have come to help.
Hibino:I use musical spells to treat precious metals. Through this I may strengthen your armor.
Hibino:Armor fragments are hidden throughout this castle. Find them and bring them here.
Europa:I think I might have what you're looking for…
Hibino:These will make quite the improvement. Let us begin.
Europa:I don't own any armor…
Europa:This dress is all I have.
Hibino:Do not fret, remnants of the ancient civilizations yet linger.
Hibino:Scarce as they may be, I recommend you search about the castle.
Hibino:Should you find one and bring it to me, I will use my magic to aid you.
Europa:I'll be sure to come back if I find anything, thank you.
Hibino:I'm afraid you don't have enough materials for me to work with.
Hibino:Let me know if you find anything interesting!
Hibino:Welcome back! Is there anything I can enhance for you?
Europa:I haven't acquired any armor yet.
Hibino:Worry not, young warrior.
Hibino:Should you find any armor, I will use my magic to aid you.
???:Oh no. Another hallucination.
Europa:What?
???:You look so real, though.
???:But no, surely you don't exist… just like those penguins I was talking to a minute ago.
Louis:Right, Louis? Yes! definitely!
Louis:What’s up, little fella!
Louis:Haha… a flying teddy bear. Very cool.
Europa:Sorry, I don’t have time for this.
Europa:We have to get you out of here. This area is very dangerous.
Louis:I know, right?
Louis:If I can be honest with you, I never thought this was going to be how my visit to the giant would turn out.
Europa:That makes two of us.
Louis:I mean, of course I wanted to come; who wouldn’t? It’s a freaking giant!
Europa:So uh… how long have you been down here?
Louis:I've been running away from monsters for… days?
Louis:I can't tell anymore. It's been a blur ever since I lost my drumsticks.
Louis:Now, all I have is this old pair. They suck, honestly.
Europa:We should really go before another monster shows up.
Louis:No way! We have to get rid of all these bad guys and rescue my drumsticks!
